## Body

PR #148 at 5de084c74c75ea63532bec6f4eb36a9f872092d7: enum-normalized attempt labels bound key cardinality to 180 and rendered key length to 35 bytes; seat retention caps 64 names plus overflow but record() has no address-byte cap. Service failures retain raw claimed addresses; bearer-protected ping exposes historical/refused names. Axum limits direct HTTP bodies to 2 MiB, but 64 large keys can approach 128 MiB, and no universal internal-address bound is established. Cardinality is not a small byte ceiling; same authentication does not mean no new data projection. Security passes with these notes, not a clearance of correctness/performance accounting blocks. No local tests; Linux CI does not execute macOS observers. Evidence: security/outputs/2026-11/07-verdict-pr-148-5de084c.dd.json.
